restatements.text: Titles the measure the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.
Titles the measure the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.

States findings that federal and state funding cuts threaten Medi-Cal, public education, and food assistance programs, and asserts that a one-time 5 percent wealth tax on billionaires is a fair way to raise revenue.
Declares the purpose is to protect health care, public education, and food assistance by taxing billionaires' wealth, which it states is often untaxed.

Amends the Constitution to authorize the billionaire wealth tax, creates the 2026 Billionaire Tax Reserve Fund to hold the revenue, allocates it 90 percent to health and 10 percent to education and food assistance, and exempts the fund from state spending limits and standard general fund requirements.

Specifies allowable uses for the health and education and food assistance accounts, authorizes the Legislature to appropriate up to $25 billion annually, provides a $50 million start-up loan to the Franchise Tax Board, and requires annual reporting on the fund.
Titles the statutory portion of the measure the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act.

Imposes a 5 percent excise tax in 2026 on the net worth of individuals and trusts with a net worth of $1 billion or more, with a phase-in for those near the threshold, and tasks the Franchise Tax Board with examining returns.

Defines how debts and liabilities are calculated for net worth, fully counting recourse debts but limiting nonrecourse debts to collateral value, and restricting deductions for pledges to charities or debts owed to related persons.

evidence.quote: In the case of debts other than recourse debts described in subdivision (a), for each such debt or liability, the amount that may be taken into account shall not exceed the amounts included in the taxpayer’s net worth on account of the assets serving as collateral for the debt or liability.
evidence.why: The measure creates complex new rules for calculating net worth by limiting which debts can be deducted based on whether they are recourse or nonrecourse.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more, and on applicable trusts.
evidence.why: The measure imposes a new tax specifically on individuals with a net worth of $1 billion or more, increasing the share of taxes paid by the wealthiest residents.

evidence.quote: The Board shall examine all returns submitted in accordance with this Part and shall determine the correct amount of the tax under this Part. The Board shall also examine all certifications or returns of taxpayers when the Board reasonably believes the taxpayers should have paid the tax imposed by this Part. Without limiting any other powers of the Board, in examining the returns made by taxpayers and examining whether returns should have been made by taxpayers but were not, the Board has all powers provided in Section 19504.
evidence.why: The measure expands the Franchise Tax Board's authority to examine returns and determine the correct tax for individuals subject to the new net worth tax.

evidence.quote: Ninety percent shall be allocated to the Billionaire Tax Health Account for health care funding, which may include expenditures to restore or address any reductions in federal funding or state appropriations; investments to protect or enhance Medi-Cal and other health coverage programs for low-and moderate-income individuals
evidence.why: The measure directs 90 percent of the new fund to health care, including investments in Medi-Cal and safety net providers.

evidence.quote:
the Department of Finance, in consultation with relevant state agencies, shall provide to the Legislature all the following information:
(1) The current balance in the Reserve Fund as of the reporting date;
evidence.why: The measure requires annual reports to the Legislature detailing the Reserve Fund's balance, estimated revenues, and proposed expenditures.

evidence.quote: All revenues from the Act—including taxes, interest, and penalties, and less refunds—shall be deposited in the State Treasury by the State Controller to the credit of the Reserve Fund. After accounting for administrative expenses as provided by law, the Controller shall allocate and transfer the remaining moneys in the Reserve Fund to the following sub-accounts, which are hereby created: 90% to the Billionaire Tax Health Account and 10% to the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account.
evidence.why: The measure guarantees that all revenues from the new tax are deposited into a special fund and automatically allocated to health, education, and food assistance accounts.

evidence.quote: “Appropriations subject to limitation” of each entity of government and the state under Article XIIIB shall not include appropriations of revenue from the Reserve Fund. No adjustment in the appropriations limit of any entity of government shall be required pursuant to Section 3 of Article XIIIB as a result of revenue being deposited in or appropriated from the Reserve Fund.
evidence.why: The measure exempts the new tax revenues from the state's constitutional spending limit, giving the state more flexibility to spend the money.

evidence.quote: moneys in the Reserve Fund shall not be borrowed, loaned, or otherwise transferred to the General Fund or any other state or local fund or account. Moneys deposited into the Reserve Fund shall only be used for the specific purposes provided by law.
evidence.why: The measure locks the new tax revenues into a special fund for specific purposes and prohibits transferring them to the General Fund.

evidence.quote:
Ten percent shall be allocated to the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account for education-related and food assistance expenditures, which may include:
(A) Education-related expenditures to restore or address any reductions in federal funding or state appropriations, or to make investments to protect or enhance the kindergarten through grade fourteen public education system.
evidence.why: The measure dedicates a portion of the tax revenue to expenditures that protect or enhance the public education system from kindergarten through grade 14.

evidence.quote: The Legislature shall have the authority to appropriate up to $22.5 billion each fiscal year from the Billionaire Tax Health Account and up to $2.5 billion each year from the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account.
evidence.why: The measure allows the state to spend up to $25 billion per year from the new accounts to fund health care, education, and food assistance.

The Board shall also examine all certifications or returns of taxpayers when the Board reasonably believes the taxpayers should have paid the tax imposed by this Part. Without limiting any other powers of the Board, in examining the returns made by taxpayers and examining whether returns should have been made by taxpayers but were not, the Board has all powers provided in Section 19504.
evidence.why: The measure creates a new tax and grants the Franchise Tax Board the power to audit returns and certifications related to it.

evidence.quote: An excise tax is imposed for tax year 2026 on the activity of sustaining excessive accumulations of wealth by applicable individuals with net worth of $1 billion dollars ($1,000,000,000) or more, and on applicable trusts.
evidence.why: The measure imposes a new tax on individuals who have a net worth of $1 billion or more.

analysis.answer: Current law was not provided. The measure creates the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act, imposing a one-time 5 percent excise tax in 2026 on the net worth of California residents with $1 billion or more. It limits how certain debts reduce net worth for this calculation. It establishes a new Reserve Fund continuously splitting the revenue—90 percent to a health account and 10 percent to an education and food assistance account—exempting it from the state's appropriations limit and Proposition 98 calculations.

The measure authorizes up to $50 million for the Franchise Tax Board's start-up costs for administration and evaluation, which would later be repaid with tax collections. Compliance costs for taxpayers with over $1 billion in net worth would likely be significant, as calculating net worth and distinguishing qualifying debts involves complex appraisals. There may be opportunity costs if wealth leaves the state or if investment patterns change to minimize the tax.

Individuals and trusts with a net worth of $1 billion or more pay the tax. The funds primarily benefit low- and moderate-income Californians by supporting Medi-Cal, public schools (K-14), CalFresh, and food banks, and the safety net providers, schools, and administrators serving those systems. The Franchise Tax Board also receives funding for administration.

Billionaires may attempt to restructure assets, shift residency out of California prior to the tax date, or use optional deferral accounts to manage the liability. The Franchise Tax Board will need to hire experts, create new forms, and conduct complex audits to enforce the tax. Healthcare providers and school districts may use the funding to plug budget holes or expand services depending on how the Legislature appropriates the money.

The measure addresses stated threats of federal and state funding cuts to Medi-Cal, education, and food assistance, as well as wealth inequality where billionaires pay a smaller percentage of their economic income in taxes than average earners. The mechanism reaches this by imposing a targeted wealth tax on billionaires and legally walling off the revenue exclusively for health, education, and food programs.

The Franchise Tax Board gains significant new authority and discretion to audit wealth valuations and administer the tax. The Legislature gains the authority to appropriate up to $25 billion annually from the newly created accounts. The Department of Finance gains the role of determining when the Reserve Fund can be abolished and evaluating funding needs.

The behavioral effects of wealth taxes—such as capital flight, tax avoidance, and the impact on investment and state revenues—are disputed. Some researchers find that wealth taxes lead to significant relocation or asset sheltering by the ultra-wealthy, while others argue that carefully designed state-level wealth taxes can raise substantial revenue with minimal economic harm.

The measure provides an initial $50 million start-up loan to the Franchise Tax Board for administration, which is to be repaid from the revenues. Ongoing annual administrative costs will be reimbursed from the Reserve Fund, but the exact total is unknown and depends on the scale of enforcement, audits, and litigation needed to collect the tax.

The measure amends the California Constitution and statutes. Undoing the constitutional provisions would generally require another ballot measure approved by voters. The Reserve Fund can be abolished by the Legislature only after the Department of Finance determines all revenues have been collected and spent.

flags.quote: Other reductions in federal funding that threaten or cause reductions in Medi-Cal or other health care coverage, access, benefits, funding, programs, services and payments to providers that affect low- and moderate-income individuals, or to statewide education or food assistance funding, or to the health care safety net more generally.
flags.note: The definition of "reductions in federal funding" is open-ended.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of the Constitution, the Act provides for taxation on all forms of personal property and wealth
flags.note: Overrides other constitutional limits on taxing property or wealth.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, the Reserve Fund is a special fund
flags.note: Overrides other laws regarding fund designation.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding Section 16305.7 of the Government Code, any interest or dividends earned on moneys in the Reserve Fund shall be retained in the Reserve Fund
flags.note: Overrides a specific government code section regarding interest.

flags.quote: Notwithstanding Section 32 or any other provision of law, a facial challenge to the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act is authorized to be adjudicated through a validation action
flags.note: Overrides existing limits on pre-payment tax challenges.

flags.quote: The Legislature shall have the authority to appropriate up to $22.5 billion each fiscal year from the Billionaire Tax Health Account and up to $2.5 billion each year from the Billionaire Tax Education and Food Assistance Account.
flags.note: The actual spending of the funds depends on future legislative appropriations.

flags.note: Sets the tax year for the imposition of the tax.
